description:
Determine whether byte-oriented $\mathrm{GF}(2^8)$ arithmetic improves existing vector and matrix consumers after all conversion costs.

## Background

FieldVec::axpy and batched FieldMatrix operations are concrete library consumers; their current element representation can make byte packing expensive. A region multiply-XOR microbenchmark alone does not justify a new production API or storage redesign.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Satisfy the [Zen 3 measurement contract](dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/measurement-contract.md) for correctness, reproducible release benchmarks, comparison validity and adoption; receipts pin its committed version, the frozen protocol and the cell addendum. Include mandatory before/after evidence for production changes and preserve negative outcomes.

- [hard] REQ-02: Publish profiles and baseline receipts for FieldVec::axpy and representative batched FieldMatrix operations, identifying time shares, coefficient reuse, current representation and actual accelerated path. Distinguish vector, matrix and any demonstrated region-shaped workload rather than assuming one kernel serves all three.

- [hard] REQ-03: Compare matching matrix cells against pinned M4RIE and matching fixed-coefficient region cells against ISA-L/GF-Complete only when a measured consumer has those semantics. Preserve field polynomial/basis and output accumulation; include 0x11B versus 0x11D incompatibility explicitly.

- [hard] REQ-04: Evaluate bounded prototypes only after profiling and MSRV feasibility evidence. Measure table preparation, reuse counts, u64/byte input conversion, output conversion, allocation and whole-consumer cost against the current implementation; keep arbitrary independent multiplication as a separate control.

- [hard] REQ-05: Validate candidate arithmetic with the shared field-law/backend contract, all byte coefficients for affected polynomials, zero/one coefficients, unaligned inputs, tails and documented overlap behavior.

- [hard] REQ-06: Publish a proceed/no-proceed decision under the frozen effect and complexity rules. Defer byte-region APIs and packing redesign unless measured consumer benefit justifies them; any positive production proposal has a reviewed library-layer design and explicitly tracked implementation scope before shipping. No qualifying prototype is a valid outcome; measurements and explanation are mandatory.

## Notes

This task owns consumer profiles and feasibility evidence, not an unconditional region API or a presumed byte-packed matrix redesign.



Source references: [IsaL2026], [GfComplete2026], [Mfourrie2026].
